extracted.intended_audience: Mathematicians participating in AMS sectional meetings (speakers, organizers, and attendees)
extracted.subtask_short: AMS sectional meeting submissions and logistics
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for participating in American Mathematical Society (AMS) sectional meetings: submitting abstracts for invited/special/contributed sessions, session organization, registration, accommodations, travel, and local logistics. Covers deadlines, presentation lengths, fees, and organizer timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of invited addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited addresses at Sectional Meetings are selected by the Section Program Committee, usually twelve to eighteen months in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members wishing to nominate candidates for invited addresses should send the relevant information to the Associate Secretary for the Section, who will forward it to the Section Program Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for abstracts for invited addresses and special sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts for consideration for invited addresses and special sessions must be submitted by the published deadline (example given: July 13, 1992).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deadline is published in the Calendar of AMS Meetings and Conferences and in the Invited Speakers and Special Sessions section of the Notices; compliance with the stated deadline is required for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributed papers abstract deadline and late-paper policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts for contributed sessions (ten-minute and other contributed papers) must be submitted by the stated deadline (example given: August 3, 1992).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late papers will not be accommodated. Submitters must meet the published deadline to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and lengths of presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings include invited one-hour addresses, selected twenty-minute special-session papers, and contributed ten-minute papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special sessions are organized as selected twenty-minute papers by invitation of the program committee; contributed papers are accommodated in ten-minute slots where announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special sessions are by invitation and organized topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Special sessions are held by invitation of the Section Program Committee and consist of selected twenty-minute papers on organized topics with named organizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers propose topics and are listed with the session; the Notices publishes the topics and organizers. Abstracts for these sessions must meet the special-session submission deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and timetable for organizers of special sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a timetable for announcing and organizing Special Sessions (deadlines for organizers and for consideration of abstracts); these deadlines are published in the Notices and the Information for Organizers section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers must meet the published organizer and consideration deadlines (examples: 'Deadline for organizers: Expired', 'Deadline for consideration: September 17, 1992' for a future meeting) to have sessions listed and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration fees and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration fees are published and categorized (example: $30 for AMS members, $45 for nonmembers, $10 for students or unemployed mathematicians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees and registration desk hours/locations are published for each meeting; registrants should follow the stated procedures and hours when registering at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration desk location and hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Each meeting lists where and when the registration desk will be open (examples: Dayton — first floor lobby of Russ Engineering Center: 12:30–5:00 p.m. Friday, 8:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. Saturday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendees should register during the published hours and at the stated location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hotel block reservations and conference rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Rooms are blocked at specific hotels for meeting participants; participants should make their own reservations and ask for the AMS conference rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS is not responsible for rate changes or the quality of the accommodations. Deadlines for reservations and the quoted rates (flat rates, single/double pricing) are published for each hotel; participants should verify street addresses and reservation deadlines when booking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hotel reservation deadlines and confirmation details
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed hotel has a reservation deadline and quoted rates (examples: Comfort Inn deadline Oct 16; Holiday Inn deadline Oct 9; Homewood Suites deadline Oct 9; Red Roof Inn deadline Oct 20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making reservations participants should mention the AMS confirmation number when provided (example: Red Roof Inn confirmation number: 205AA92304). Rates and deadlines are binding for obtaining the blocked rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes and AMS responsibility for accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hotel rates are subject to local taxes (example: all rates subject to a twelve percent tax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS disclaims responsibility for rate changes or the quality of the accommodations; participants accept hotel policies and taxes when booking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parking policies at meeting venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking availability and rules are published for each meeting (examples: Dayton — free parking available to participants in specified campus lots; Los Angeles — parking permits required and cost $5 per day, park in Parking Structure A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should follow the published parking instructions (lots designated, permit requirements, nearest structures) and note exceptions (reserved spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Food service and local dining information
rubrics_metrics.description: On-campus cafeterias and nearby restaurants/fast-food outlets and their hours are listed for participants' convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific dining facilities, hours (e.g., cafeteria open for breakfast, lunch, dinner on certain days), and campus amenities (e.g., Commons Cafeteria, Cafe 84) are provided; attendees should plan meals according to these schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel directions and alternate routing notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed driving directions from major highways and alternate routes are provided; construction or route changes may require following alternate directions (example: Ohio Route 4 construction alters approach recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants arriving by air are given airport information, car-rental and ground-transportation contacts, approximate drive times, and shuttle options; follow published alternates if usual routes are under construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local attractions and weather guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings provide local weather averages and nearby attractions (example: Dayton — US Air Force Museum; Los Angeles — museums near campus) as helpful contextual information for attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practical notes such as museum hours/admission and campus gym/pool access policies (e.g., pool/gym use with meeting badge and fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of invited addresses and special sessions list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notices publishes lists of invited addresses and the information about Special Sessions that is available at printing time; invited addresses and special-session information are announced in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some meeting listings may be incomplete; for full nomination or speaker submission procedures, contact the Associate Secretary for the Section.
